There isn’t a single “Dr. Karp” who is universally known—several real‑world scholars and a few fictional characters share that name. Below are the most common references, so you can tell which one you’re looking for (or let me know if you had someone else in mind). --- ## 1. **Richard M. Karp – Computer‑Science Legend** | Detail | Information | |--------|-------------| | **Full name** | Richard Manning Karp | | **Title** | Professor of Computer Science, University of California, Berkeley | | **Field** | Algorithms, computational complexity, combinatorial optimization | | **Key achievements** | • **Turing Award (1985)** – “for his contributions to the theory of algorithms, especially for his work on NP‑completeness and efficient algorithms for combinatorial problems.”
• Developed **Karp’s 21 NP‑complete problems** (1972), a cornerstone of complexity theory.
• Invented the **Karp–Miller–Rosenberg algorithm** for network flow, the **Hopcroft–Karp algorithm** for maximum bipartite matching, and many other classic algorithms.
• Co‑author of the seminal textbook *“Algorithm Design”* (with Steven Levitin). | | **Notable publications** | • “Reducibility among combinatorial problems” (1972) – introduced the 21 NP‑complete problems.
• “Maximum flow in a network with multiple sources and sinks” (1973). | | **Current status** | Emeritus professor; still active in research, mentoring, and public talks. | | **Why people ask about him** | He is one of the most cited computer‑science researchers ever, and his name appears on many algorithmic concepts (e.g., **Karp’s algorithm**, **Karp–Miller–Rosenberg**, **Karp–Sipser**). | --- ## 2. **Dr. Karp in Popular Culture** | Work | Character | Role | |------|-----------|------| | **“The Simpsons”** (episode “The Springfield Files”) | Dr. **Karp** | A brief cameo as a scientist who comments on a UFO sighting. | | **“The Walking Dead”** (comic/TV) | Dr. **Karp** | Minor medical staff member at the CDC in early story arcs. | | **“The Big Bang Theory”** (season 5, episode “The Shiny Trinket”) | Dr. **Karp** | A visiting professor who critiques Sheldon’s paper. | | **“Star Trek: Voyager”** (novel *The Eternal Tide*) | Dr. **Karp** | A xenobiologist who studies a new alien species. | These appearances are usually one‑off jokes or background roles, so they rarely have a deep backstory. --- ## 3. **Other Real‑World Dr. Karp(s)** | Name | Field | Notable Fact | |------|-------|--------------| | **Dr. Miriam Karp** | Oncology (Harvard Medical School) | Research on targeted therapies for breast cancer. | | **Dr. David Karp** | Neuroscience (University of Chicago) | Known for work on synaptic plasticity. | | **Dr. Ellen Karp** | Environmental Engineering (MIT) | Pioneered sustainable water‑treatment technologies. | If you heard the name in a scientific paper, conference, or news article, it’s most likely one of these researchers (or Richard Karp, if the context is algorithms). --- ## 4. **How to Pin It Down** - **If the context is computer science, algorithms, or the Turing Award →** you’re almost certainly talking about **Richard M. Karp**. - **If the context is a TV show, movie, or comic book →** it’s probably a **fictional Dr. Karp** (see the table above). - **If the context is medicine, biology, or engineering →** it could be one of the other academic Dr. Karps listed. --- ### Quick “Did you mean…?” Checklist 1. **Algorithmic theory / NP‑completeness?** → Richard Karp. 2. **A cameo in a sitcom or cartoon?** → One of the fictional Dr. Karps. 3. **Medical research or a hospital?** → Likely a medical Dr. Karp (Miriam, David, Ellen, etc.). If none of these match, feel free to give me a bit more detail (e.g., the field, the medium, or a quote you saw) and I’ll narrow it down for you!
